Marcus — thanks for the demo last week. Legal has a few follow-ups on the DPA before we can proceed with procurement. High-level asks: 

- Please confirm Redwood's role(s) under the DPA specifically for: (a) raw customer content sent to the API; (b) embeddings derived from that content; (c) telemetry/logs collected for debugging & quality. Who is Controller vs Processor for each?
- We need the current subprocessor list and your process for notice/opt-out (or objection).
- What data transfer mechanism do you rely on for EU->US processing (SCCs, adequacy, Binding Corporate Rules)?
- Can you provide a redline of the DPA that clarifies retention windows for request/trace logs and a clause preventing use of embeddings for model training without explicit consent?
- Finally, can you confirm how you'd like to sign (DocuSign preferred) and a target countersign date — our procurement wants to close by next Friday.

I've attached Acme's standard DPA template for reference (sent separately). Please respond with short, actionable answers — we can iterate on wording but want to avoid open-ended language.

Sarah — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Short answers here, then I attach a proposed redline and the subprocessor notice link. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

1) Roles (short): Redwood is the processor for customer content you send to our inference API; you (Acme) are the controller. This also applies to embeddings generated by the service: Redwood processes and stores embeddings on behalf of Acme under controller instructions.

2) Telemetry / logs: Redwood collects request metadata and limited telemetry (timestamps, token counts, error traces) to operate and improve the service. We treat debugging logs as processor-held operational logs. Retention: default operational logs 30 days, extended audit logs 12 months (can be negotiated for enterprise plans). We do not use request-level content or embeddings for model training unless a customer opts in.

3) Subprocessors: we publish a current list and give 30 days' notice before onboarding critical subprocessors. Link: https://status.redwood.com/subprocessors/list-2026-03-10 (attached PDF).

4) EU data transfers: Redwood relies on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for controller-processor transfers and complements them with technical controls (encryption at-rest/in-transit, region pinning where available). For customers requiring additional contractual safeguards we can add the SCCs schedule and a documented transfer impact assessment.

5) Redline & signing: attached is our proposed DPA redline that: (a) states Redwood is processor; (b) codifies the 30-day/12-month retention buckets; (c) adds a no-training-without-consent clause for embeddings; (d) includes reference to SCCs and subprocessors notice. We typically execute via DocuSign — I can send a DocuSign envelope if you confirm the counterparty name and signer. Target: countersign by Fri, 19 Mar to meet your procurement ask.

Attached: ACME_DPA_proposed_redline_v1.docx, redwood_subprocessors_list_20260310.pdf

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Partnerships (Redwood Inference)

Marcus — quick legal notes on the proposed redline before you send externally: 

- Controller/Processor language: keep Redwood as "Processor" with explicit callout that customers are Controllers for their content and derived artifacts (embeddings). Adding a short example sentence helps (e.g., "Customer instructs Processor to generate embeddings from Customer Content and Processor acts only on Customer's instructions").
- Telemetry: change "request-level content" wording to "customer content" (to avoid ambiguity). Add explicit carve-out that aggregated/anonymous telemetry may be used for service improvement.
- Retention: confirm the buckets you quoted (30d operational, 12mo audit) in the DPA body and include an escalation route for customers to request shorter retention for regulated data.
- No-training clause: tighten to "Processor will not use Customer Content or derived embeddings to improve model parameters or training datasets without prior written consent."
- Subprocessors: we should keep the 30-day notice and add an objection mechanism for critical subprocessors (Customer may object in writing within 20 days).
- EU transfers: confirm SCCs schedule is attached and add a statement that both parties will cooperate on any DPIA or regulator request.

I've marked these changes in the attached redline (ACME_DPA_proposed_redline_v1.docx). Once Marcus posts the DocuSign envelope, have Naomi (privacy) review the final envelope language.
